Diagnose Cross-Dataset Variable Attribute Consistency

Source: R/variable_attribute_consistency.R
variable_attribute_consistency.Rd

Produces a descriptive, tidy report of variables whose data attributes drift across the datasets in which they appear. A variable name that is used in more than one dataset (for example USUBJID in ADSL and ADAE) is expected to carry the same data type, storage length, and display format everywhere; a mismatch is a common, objective source of reviewer friction and a frequent cause of transport-file surprises.

Usage

variable_attribute_consistency(
  metadata,
  attributes = c("type", "length", "format")
)

Arguments

metadata

A data frame with at least columns dataset (character) and variable (character), plus any of the attribute columns named in attributes. Compatible with the adam_metadata, sdtm_metadata, and oncology_metadata datasets from r4subdata.

attributes

A character vector naming the attribute columns to check for cross-dataset consistency. Defaults to c("type", "length", "format"). Any name not present in metadata is skipped.

Value

A tibble with one row per finding and the columns:

finding_type

One of "inconsistent_type", "inconsistent_length", or "inconsistent_format" (one per checked attribute).

variable

The variable whose attribute is inconsistent.

dataset

The dataset this row reports.

attribute

The name of the attribute column involved.

value

The attribute value this variable carries in this dataset (as character).

detail

A human-readable description of the finding.

When every shared variable is consistent, a zero-row tibble with the same columns is returned.

Details

Like label_consistency() and variable_name_conformance(), and unlike the scored usability indicators (for example assess_label_quality()), this function does not score anything or emit R4SUB evidence rows; it is a purely advisory diagnostic. The result is tidy: one row per affected dataset occurrence per attribute, so a variable that differs on both type and length appears under two finding types. The following finding types may be emitted, one per checked attribute column that is present in metadata:

inconsistent_type

The type attribute differs across datasets.

inconsistent_length

The length attribute differs across datasets.

inconsistent_format

The format attribute differs across datasets.

Only the attribute columns named in attributes that are actually present in metadata are checked; requested attributes that are absent are silently skipped, so the function is safe to call on metadata that carries only some of them. Values are compared after trimming leading and trailing white space; NA and empty-string values are treated as missing and never drive a finding, so a variable that simply lacks (say) a format in one dataset is not reported.

See also

label_consistency() for label-level consistency and variable_name_conformance() for name conformance.

Examples

meta <- data.frame(
  dataset  = c("ADSL", "ADAE", "ADSL", "ADAE"),
  variable = c("USUBJID", "USUBJID", "AGE", "AGE"),
  type     = c("Char", "Char", "Num", "Char"),
  length   = c(20, 40, 8, 8),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
# USUBJID differs in length; AGE differs in type.
variable_attribute_consistency(meta)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   finding_type        variable dataset attribute value detail                   
#>   <chr>               <chr>    <chr>   <chr>     <chr> <chr>                    
#> 1 inconsistent_length USUBJID  ADAE    length    40    variable 'USUBJID' has 2…
#> 2 inconsistent_length USUBJID  ADSL    length    20    variable 'USUBJID' has 2…
#> 3 inconsistent_type   AGE      ADAE    type      Char  variable 'AGE' has 2 dis…
#> 4 inconsistent_type   AGE      ADSL    type      Num   variable 'AGE' has 2 dis…

# Restrict the check to a single attribute.
variable_attribute_consistency(meta, attributes = "type")
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   finding_type      variable dataset attribute value detail                     
#>   <chr>             <chr>    <chr>   <chr>     <chr> <chr>                      
#> 1 inconsistent_type AGE      ADAE    type      Char  variable 'AGE' has 2 disti…
#> 2 inconsistent_type AGE      ADSL    type      Num   variable 'AGE' has 2 disti…
